title: Airspace Classes & Requirements
description: Flashcards covering US airspace classifications, weather minimums, and entry requirements

cards.back: 18,000 feet MSL to FL600 (60,000 feet)

• IFR flight plan required
• ATC clearance required
• Two-way radio communications
• Transponder with Mode C
• Instrument rated pilot
Surface to 10,000 feet MSL. Individually tailored to each location (often described as 'upside-down wedding cake').

• ATC clearance required (not just communication)
• Transponder with Mode C
• Two-way radio
• Private pilot certificate minimum (student with endorsement at some airports)

• Visibility: 3 statute miles
• Cloud clearance: Clear of clouds

• Core: Surface to 4,000 ft AGL, 5 NM radius
• Shelf: 1,200 to 4,000 ft AGL, 5-10 NM radius
• Outer area: 10-20 NM (services available)

• Two-way radio communication established (not clearance)
• Transponder with Mode C
• Note: Communication established when ATC responds with your callsign

• Visibility: 3 statute miles
• Cloud clearance: 500 ft below, 1,000 ft above, 2,000 ft horizontal
Surface to 2,500 feet AGL, typically 4-5 NM radius (tailored for instrument procedures)

• Two-way radio communication established
• No transponder requirement (unless in Mode C veil)
• Reverts to Class E or G when tower closed

• Visibility: 3 statute miles
• Cloud clearance: 500 ft below, 1,000 ft above, 2,000 ft horizontal

• Surface area (dashed magenta line)
• 700 ft AGL floor (magenta vignette)
• 1,200 ft AGL floor (blue vignette)
• 14,500 ft MSL floor (no vignette)
• Federal airways (Victor airways)

• Visibility: 3 statute miles
• Cloud clearance: 500 ft below, 1,000 ft above, 2,000 ft horizontal

• Visibility: 5 statute miles
• Cloud clearance: 1,000 ft below, 1,000 ft above, 1 statute mile horizontal
Uncontrolled airspace - that portion of airspace not designated as Class A, B, C, D, or E. No ATC services provided.

• Visibility: 1 statute mile
• Cloud clearance: Clear of clouds

• Visibility: 3 statute miles
• Cloud clearance: 500 ft below, 1,000 ft above, 2,000 ft horizontal

cards.front: Class GVFR Minimums (>1,200 AGL, <10,000 MSL, Day)
cards.back:
• Visibility: 1 statute mile
• Cloud clearance: 500 ft below, 1,000 ft above, 2,000 ft horizontal
Flight is prohibited. Established for security or national welfare. No exceptions for civilian aircraft. Example: P-56 Washington DC.
Flight is subject to restrictions. Contains hazardous activities (artillery, aerial gunnery, missiles). Permission may be obtained from controlling agency when not active.
Similar to restricted areas but over international waters (3+ NM from coast). US has no jurisdiction to restrict flight. Exercise extreme caution.
Separates military training from IFR traffic. VFR traffic is permitted but should exercise extreme caution. IFR may be cleared through if separation can be provided.
High volume of pilot training or unusual aerial activity. All aircraft permitted. Pilots should be alert.
Not charted because activities are suspended immediately when aircraft approach. Spotters, radar, or ground lookouts monitor for aircraft.
30 NM radius around Class B airports. Transponder with Mode C (altitude reporting) required for all aircraft.

• Request clearance from ATC
• 1 statute mile visibility
• Clear of clouds
• Some airports prohibit SVFR (Part 91 Appendix D)

• All day SVFR requirements plus:
• Pilot must be instrument rated
• Aircraft must be IFR equipped
Class E airspace with a floor of 700 feet AGL (fading magenta shading)
Class E airspace with a floor of 1,200 feet AGL (fading blue shading)
Class E airspace extending to the surface (typically around airports with instrument approaches but no operating tower)
Class B airspace boundary
Class C airspace boundary
Class D airspace boundary
Temporarily restricts aircraft operations in a defined area. Published as NOTAMs. Common reasons: disaster relief, VIP movement, special events, hazardous conditions.

• IR routes: IFR
• VR routes: VFR
• 4-digit number: below 1,500 AGL
• 3-digit number: above 1,500 AGL
Exercise extreme caution when crossing.
Radar service available but participation is voluntary. VFR pilots receive sequencing, traffic advisories, and safety alerts if participating.
250 knots indicated airspeed maximum (unless minimum safe airspeed is higher)

cards.front: Speed Limit in Class B Airspace
cards.back: 250 knots indicated airspeed maximum

cards.front: Speed Limit: Class C/D within 4 NM at/below 2,500 AGL
cards.back: 200 knots indicated airspeed maximum

cards.front: Speed Limit Underlying Class B Airspace
cards.back: 200 knots indicated airspeed maximum

A > B > C > D > E > G

When airspace overlaps, the MORE restrictive rules apply.

Memory aid: 'A Better Class Delivers Every Good pilot'

Heading 0°-179° (Eastbound):
• Odd thousands + 500 ft (3,500, 5,500, 7,500...)

Heading 180°-359° (Westbound):
• Even thousands + 500 ft (4,500, 6,500, 8,500...)

Applies above 3,000 ft AGL through FL290

IR = IFR routes
VR = VFR routes

Route numbers:
• 4 digits (IR1234): All segments at/below 1,500 AGL
• 3 digits (IR123): One or more segments above 1,500 AGL

Exercise extreme caution when crossing MTRs!

cards.front: Class B Primary Airports - Student Pilot Restrictions
cards.back:
Students PROHIBITED from solo operations at these 12 airports:
• Andrews AFB, Atlanta, Boston Logan
• Chicago O'Hare, DFW, LAX
• Miami, Newark, JFK, LaGuardia
• Reagan National (DCA), San Francisco

Other Class B airports: Student with endorsement OK

VFR FLYWAY:
• General flight path around Class B
• NO clearance required
• Depicted on TAC chart reverse

VFR CORRIDOR:
• 'Hole' through Class B
• NO clearance required
• Defined vertical/lateral limits

VFR TRANSITION ROUTE:
• Through Class B
• ATC clearance REQUIRED

• Protect persons/property from surface hazard
• Safe environment for disaster relief aircraft
• Prevent congestion of sightseeing aircraft
• Protect declared national disasters (Hawaii)
• Protect President/VP/public figures
• Space agency operations

Published via NOTAM - always check before flight!

Two-way communication ESTABLISHED when:
• ATC responds with YOUR aircraft callsign

Communication NOT established if:
• ATC says 'Aircraft calling, standby'
• ATC doesn't use your callsign

Don't enter Class C until communication established!

Part-time Class D reverts to:
• Class E surface area (if instrument procedures exist), OR
• Class G airspace

Check Chart Supplement for:
• 'Other times CLASS E'
• 'Other times CLASS G'

Overlying Class E transition area remains

REGULATORY (14 CFR Part 71/73):
• Class A, B, C, D, E
• Prohibited Areas (P)
• Restricted Areas (R)

NON-REGULATORY:
• Military Operations Areas (MOA)
• Warning Areas (W)
• Alert Areas (A)
• Controlled Firing Areas (CFA)
• National Security Areas (NSA)

• At airports without operating tower
• Has instrument procedures
• Weather observation capability required
• Communication with surface required
• Extends to adjacent/overlying controlled airspace

Chart: Dashed magenta line around airport
